obligation: Report of suspected gateway credential compromise to Client B
citation: Client B Vendor Access Agreement VAA-B (4) (supports Client B's CIP-003-9 R2 Attachment 1 Section 6)
trigger: Suspected compromise of the Client B gateway credentials, including an MFA push the owner did not start
deadline: Immediately
notify: Client B system operations desk (24x7), by phone
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term

obligation: Incident notice to Client B
citation: Client B Vendor Access Agreement VAA-B (5) (supports Client B's CIP-003-9 R2 Attachment 1 Section 4)
trigger: Any incident that may affect Client B systems or information
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term

obligation: Incident notice to Client A
citation: Client A Supplier Security Addendum SSA-A (5) (flows down CIP-013-2 R1 Parts 1.2.1 and 1.2.2)
trigger: Discovery of a cyber security incident affecting Client A information or services, including exposure of Client A BCSI
deadline: Within 24 hours of discovery; then cooperate in the response
notify: Client A security and NERC compliance contact (phone and email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term

obligation: Notice that an authorized individual no longer needs BCSI access
citation: Client A SSA-A (4) (supports Client A's CIP-004-7 R6 Part 6.3)
trigger: A person Client A authorized (today only the owner; later a standby engineer) no longer needs access, or the owner's own credentials must be revoked
deadline: Within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract term

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Responsible Entity determines a Reportable Cyber Security Incident, or an attempt to compromise, at its high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: (High/medium impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS) Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise an applicable system; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No (directly) - the business is not a Responsible Entity. Client A decides and files; the consultant's 24-hour SSA-A (5) notice feeds it

obligation: CIP-003-9 low impact incident notification to the E-ISAC
trigger: Client B determines that an identified Cyber Security Incident is a Reportable Cyber Security Incident
deadline: Per Client B's incident response plan (the standard sets no hour count for low impact)
applies_at_this_tier: No (directly) - Client B's duty; the consultant gives Client B the facts under VAA-B (5)

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report (formerly OE-417; includes cyber events)
citation: Form DOE-417, OMB-approved ICR 202402-1901-002 (expires 2027-05-31); mandatory under 15 U.S.C. 772(b)
trigger: Electric utilities and other listed entities file when their Balancing Authority does not. Criteria 2-3 (Reportable Cyber Security Incident; cyber event interrupting operations) and 11-12 (cyber event that could affect reliability; loss of service to over 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more), among others
deadline: Within 1 hour (criteria 2-3), within 6 hours (criteria 11-12); final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business is not an electric utility; the clients decide whether to file

obligation: Report of unauthorized CEII disclosure
trigger: Any unauthorized disclosure of CEII received from FERC (Client D study models)
deadline: Promptly
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if CEII was exposed (it is kept off email and the file suite)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (here, the drafter's W-9: name and Social Security number)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the W-9 data was accessed (one individual today)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds personal information of only a few individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - far below 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: Breach of security of a system maintained by a third-party agent (the accounting SaaS provider holds the W-9 and bank data)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound from the accounting SaaS provider

obligation: State data breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an affected individual lives outside Florida. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: Notice to other clients whose data was exposed
citation: Client C contract (confidentiality clause); Client D subcontract
trigger: Client C or Client D project data accessed or sent to an unapproved party
deadline: No fixed deadline in the contracts; tell them promptly (target 24 hours)
notify: Client C and Client D project managers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract duty of confidentiality

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms; call the breach hotline before hiring any outside firm
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - $100,000 cyber sublimit

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Cyber incident, especially one aimed at a client's critical infrastructure
deadline: Day 1 (voluntary)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; helps the clients and the insurer

obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident (IC Surface-2025-01 recommends earlier notice to TSA for significant incidents)
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - no pipeline clients or work

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification
trigger: Cyber security event at an NRC power reactor licensee
deadline: 1 hour / 4 hours / 8 hours depending on event; 24-hour recordable events
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: No - no nuclear clients or work

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment (proposed)
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
